chunks: From him, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah and Salih ibn Khalid, from Abu Jamilyah, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who bought one hundred manns of gold dust from another man, and the seller did not have any of it in his possession, he (the Imam) said: 'There is no objection to it if he pays him less than what was stipulated for him.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no objection / it is permissible
key_terms.مِائَةَ مَنٍّ: One hundred manns (a unit of weight)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling gold dust that the seller does not currently possess?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of *bay' al-ma'dum* (sale of non-existent goods) by affirming that delivering a partial quantity is valid if the seller compensates the buyer for the shortfall according to the agreed stipulation. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on contractual flexibility and the binding nature of specific conditions (*shurut*) in commercial transactions, distinguishing it from strict requirements of immediate full possession.
